documentation.rationale: The identity half is strong: VIN, door-jamb build date and full option sticker are photographed and match the decode. The maintenance half is missing: no invoices for IMS, clutch/DMF, cooling, AOS or plugs. The Carfax is referenced but not provided.

condition.rationale: No fault is disclosed, and the exterior looks straight and stock in photos. There is visible interior touch-point and bolster wear, surface corrosion underneath and an aged coolant tank. Nothing about engine health is proven either way.

price_value.rationale: The current bid is far below the $21,360–$27,273 fair-value band, but this is an early-stage auction and the hammer is unknown. At a likely hammer near fair value, a recordless M96 car carries a full catch-up liability.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual with a strong point of view and resells easily, so it fits the brief on transmission and enthusiasm. The M96 engine risk and recordless catch-up make it a weaker reliable bridge, and a likely hammer sits above the ideal $10k–$19k band.

logistics.rationale: It is a New Jersey dealer car on a BaT auction with no stated PPI access before bidding. It carries a Montana title, and CA smog/registration feasibility is unconfirmed. BaT shipping is available.

ppi_focus: Borescope all six cylinders for scoring, especially 4-6
Coolant pressure test plus oil cap/expansion tank inspection for milky film (3.4 liner/porosity)
Oil filter cut and oil analysis for metal and glycol
DMF/clutch evaluation and RMS weep at engine/transaxle junction
PIWIS/Durametric scan: cam deviation values, stored codes, readiness monitors for smog
Front radiators/condensers and expansion tank seams for corrosion and leaks
Underbody rust on suspension mounts, subframe and exhaust hangers
AOS symptoms: crankcase vacuum, smoke at start
Tire date codes, control arms, toe links, engine mounts
what_would_change_verdict: A clean independent PPI with borescope, pressure test and oil analysis before close would raise condition and documentation.
Invoices showing IMS retrofit, clutch/DMF/RMS or cooling work would substantially cut the catch-up liability.
Confirmation of a CA-certified emissions label and an unbranded title would improve logistics.
Downward: a branded title, accident history in the Carfax, evidence of coolant/oil mixing or bore scoring, or no inspection access.
evidence.mission_note: A six-speed 911 coupe fits the manual enthusiast brief and resells easily, but a recordless 996.1 is not a low-risk bridge. Its fit depends on engine-health evidence and a hammer that leaves room for a $4.5k–10k catch-up.
evidence.rationale: The listing firmly establishes identity: matching VIN, door-jamb label and option sticker confirm a 2/98-build 1999 C2 coupe with the factory M96.01 engine and G96 six-speed. That early build date means a factory dual-row IMS bearing. Observed issues are limited to stated interior touch-point wear, surface corrosion underneath, and a Montana title on a New Jersey car with a possibly 2018-dated inspection sticker. No service history beyond a claimed 2026 oil change is offered. There are no records for IMS, clutch/DMF/RMS, cooling, AOS or plugs, and no borescope, oil analysis, cold-start video or smog certificate. The Carfax is referenced but not provided, so owners, accidents and the mileage trail remain open. The current $9,996 bid is an opening figure, and comps put fair value at $21,360–$27,273.
evidence.next_action: Ask Euro_Classica today for the Carfax PDF, a title photo, the full emissions-label photo, and permission for an independent PPI with borescope and coolant pressure test before the 10/29 close.
